mainEntity.name: Why does dividing complex numbers use the conjugate?

acceptedAnswer.text: Multiplying the denominator by its conjugate z̄ turns it into the real number |z|², eliminating i from the denominator — the complex equivalent of rationalizing a square root.

mainEntity.name: What is the geometric meaning of multiplying complex numbers?

acceptedAnswer.text: Multiplication multiplies the moduli and adds the arguments — geometrically, it scales and rotates. This is exactly what De Moivre's theorem generalizes to powers and roots.

mainEntity.name: Why does a complex number have n different nth roots?

acceptedAnswer.text: Because angles that differ by a full turn (2π) describe the same point, but raising to the nth power multiplies the angle by n — so n different starting angles, spaced 2π/n apart, all land on the same result.

mainEntity.name: What is the complex conjugate used for?

acceptedAnswer.text: Besides division, z·z̄ = |z|² always gives a real number, which is essential for finding magnitudes, normalizing vectors, and in signal processing for computing power from a complex amplitude.

mainEntity.name: How is Euler's formula related to polar form?

acceptedAnswer.text: Euler's formula e^(iθ) = cos θ + i sin θ lets polar form r(cos θ + i sin θ) be written compactly as r·e^(iθ) — the same number, and the form that makes multiplication, powers and roots most natural.
